questions.question:
**A sentence has been given in Direct/Indirect Speech. Out of the four given alternatives, select the one which best expresses the same sentence in Indirect/Direct Speech.**

The king said, “Alas! Our enemies are too strong.”

options.text: The king said that their enemies were too strong.
The king exclaimed sadly that their enemies were too strong.
The king was sad because the enemies were too strong.
The enemies were too strong for the king.

questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**The king exclaimed sadly that their enemies were too strong.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

While changing the narration of an exclamatory sentence, we need to follow the steps given below-

 
• An exclamatory sentence expresses a state of joy, sorrow, or wonder, to change them into Indirect Speech, specific words (i.e. exclaimed with joy, exclaimed with sorrow, exclaimed with surprise, etc.) are added to the sentence.
 
• Put "that" between the reporting and reported speeches. (it is optional to put "that" between the reporting and reported speech)
 
• Present indefinite tense in direct speech is changed into past indefinite tense in indirect speech.
 
• **'Our' **will be changed into **'their'.**

Thus, the sentence becomes: *The king exclaimed sadly that their enemies were too strong.*

questions.question: Weight of Arun is 4/7 of the weight of Bablu. Weight of Bablu is 1/2 of the weight of Ram. Weight of Ram is 4 times of the weight of Deep. Weight of Deep is 1/9 of the weight of Ankit. Whose weight is more than the weight of Deep but less than the weight of Bablu?

Let the weight of Ankit is 9x kg

Weight of Deep → 1/9 × 9x = x kg

Weight of Ram → 4 × x = 4x kg

Weight of Bablu → 4x/2 = 2x kg

Weight of Arun → 4/7 × 2x = 1.14x kg

Ankit > Ram > Bablu > Arun > Deep

As we can seen clearly, Arun’s weight is more than the weight of Deep but less than the weight of Bablu.

Hence, the correct answer is **"Arun".**

questions.question: Debenture holders of a company are its _________.
questions.solution:
The ‘debenture’ is derived from the Latin word ‘debere’ which means ‘to owe’.

 
• It is a written instrument that acknowledges a loan to the company and is executed under the company’s common seal.
 
• It contains a contract for the principal amount to be repaid after a specified period or at intervals and for payment of interest at a fixed rate which is usually paid either half-yearly or yearly on fixed dates.
 
• A person having the debentures is called debenture holder. They are the persons or firms who purchase the debentures of other company. They are not concerned with the management and regulation of the company.
 
• Debentures are usually secured and carry a charge on the assets of the company, hence, debenture holders are the secured creditors of the company.

questions.question: Which plant tissue is also known as growing tissue?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Only Meristematic tissue**__.

__
 
• Meristematic tissue is also known as growing tissue.
 
• Meristematic tissues are responsible for the growth of the plant.
 
• They consist of immature cells which have the power to divide.
 
• On the basis of their position in the plant, meristems are apical, lateral & intercalary.

 
 

 
 
Apical Meristem

 
 
 
Increase length at the tip of the plant

 
 
 

 
 
Lateral Meristem

 
 
 
Increase diameter, the thickness of the plant

 
 
 

 
 
Intercalary Meristem

 
 
 
Increase the length of organs like leaves and internodes

 
 
 

Meristematic tissue__:

 
• Growing regions of the plants are called Meristem.
 
• Meristematic tissue has the capability of cell division.
 
• It is round, oval, and multisided.
 
• It grows and constitutes the different parts of the plant.

**There are three types of meristematic tissues-**

 
• Apical meristem- these are located at the shoot tips and root tips.
 
• Intercalary meristem- located between permanent tissues, at the leaf base and nodes.
 
• Lateral meristem- located at the sides(edges).​
